checks.detail: The real UI showed the exact Harbor cache-coherency task, one reviewed Acceptance Planner plan, and successful structured-tool preflight for both Minimal Coder and Invariant Defender. Every agent used the deterministic local harbor-ways-fixture provider, so this take proves Axocoatl's execution lifecycle rather than model or provider diversity.

Route showed 5 of 7 steps diverged across two independent Podman-backed attempts: coder read lib/catalog.js, made two focused edits, then ran npm run check; defender searched the cache surface, read the contract and implementation, replaced lib/catalog.js, then ran the same check.

Both non-empty production-only candidates passed the protected npm run check contract with 6 tests passed and 0 failed. Candidate 0 changed lib/catalog.js by +2/-2 and candidate 1 by +8/-7; the immutable checked commits, trees, and exact binary-diff hashes were retained while lib/catalog.test.js remained unchanged.

Outcome and the readable changed-path view compared the same verified evidence before Judge: candidate 0 cleared the cache after each mutation, while candidate 1 attached revisions to cached results. The UI exposed each outcome, diff, duration, token usage, known-zero local fixture cost, and Route.

Evidence Judge assigned candidate 0 rank 1 and candidate 1 rank 2, with this recorded reasoning: Both candidates pass the same protected checks. The broad invalidation patch wins because it is the smallest complete coherence boundary; the revisioned strategy makes invalidation lazy but introduces extra cache-entry state.

The operator deliberately kept candidate 0. The canonical completed Turn and Keep receipt identify the same attempt set and sole touched path; the primary checkout then contained only unstaged lib/catalog.js at +2/-2, npm run check passed all 6 tests, git diff --check was clean, and temporary attempt refs, worktrees, results, and containers were cleaned without creating a commit.
